To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) high-frequency sequence boundaries in shoreface sandstones can lead to basin-scale dolomite cemementation of sandstones; 2) dolomite cementation in the shoreface was promoted by meteoric fluids migrating basinward into the shoreface during relative sea-level fall and mixing with marine porewater and the presence of a detrital dolomicrite component; and 3) this dolomite cementation can be traced basinward for tens of kilometers

(1) high-frequency sequence boundaries in the Desert Member, Book Cliff, Utah were formed during relative sea-level fall; and (2) basin-scale dolomite cements formed in shoreface sandstones downdip from high-frequency sequence boundaries as a result of mixing of marine and meteoric pore fluids and precipitation from these pore fluids in the presence of detital dolomite.

(1) the dolomite cements are restricted to a narrow interval of the upper shoreface, (2) dolomitization occurred in the uppermost part of the shoreface sandstone, where the sandstone was in contact with meteoric fluids, and (3) the source of the dolomite cemets is the leaching of dolomite detritus from coastal plain deposits that were exposed by the sea-level fall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between sea-level fall, meteoric diagenesis, and dolomite cementation.
the role of sea-level change in the development of basin-scale early diogenetic cementation in sandstones.
the relationship between stratigraphy and early diagenesis.

the formation of the concretions is a result of a combination of factors, including: 1) the presence of detrial dolomite, 2) the presence of organic-rich mudstones, 3) the presence of marine pore waters, 4) meteoric fluids, 5) the formation of a high frequency sequence boundary, and 6) the formation of an incised valley.
the formation of the ferroan dolomites in the upper shoreface sandstone of the Desert Member, Book Cliff, Utah, is a result of the interaction of the meteoric water and the detrital dolomitic grains.

the formation of dolomite concretionary bodies in the upper shoreface sandstone facies is a result of the interplay between meteoric fluids, marine pore waters, and detrital dolomites during relative sea-level falls.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dolomite cementation in the desert member is the result of a combination of sea-level fall and the detrital carbonate content of the shoreface sandstone.
the formation of dolomite cement bodies is not restricted to the coastal plain but can occur in the shoreface as well.
the development of high-frequency sequence boundary surfaces in the Desert Member led to the formation of basin-wide dolomite concretion and cement bodies.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of detrilal dolomite in shoreface sandstones can be used as a guide to the presence of meteoric fluids in these sandstones and that these meteoric fluids are a potential source of dolomite cementation in the shoreface.
dolomite cementation is a diagenetic process that is not restricted to the shallow subsurface.
dolomite precipitation can be promoted by sea-level fall, and this can occur at the scale of individual high-frequency sequence boundaries.
